messages:
From: Marta Gonzalez <marta.gonzalez@medline.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: infrastructure@medline.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood private deployment kickoff — network prerequisites

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the quick intro earlier. We're planning to kick off the private/VPC deployment for Medline next month and need your guidance to clear the networking and environment acceptance gates. To make the vendor-side procurement and network team work efficient, could you share a concise checklist of the minimum items we must provide from our side plus any smoke tests Redwood will run?

Key items our infra team asked for up front:
- Public NAT/IPs (for egress) or requirements for SNAT
- IP allowlist ranges for control-plane/API and any TLS endpoints
- Service account roles and recommended least-privilege IAM roles
- KMS/HSM integration options and required certs
- Expected ports & protocols (ingress/egress) and recommended firewall rules
- Audit log retention and log export endpoints

I've attached our internal matrix (medline-infra-requirements.xlsx) that includes current network owners and a tentative timeline.

Can we get your checklist by EOD Monday so we can schedule a readiness call with our network ops?

Thanks — Marta
Marta Gonzalez
Head of Infrastructure, Medline Health

Marta — thanks for the clear list and the matrix. I've pulled together a compact onboarding runbook that covers the "entry gate" items we need from Medline to validate an environment as production-ready. Attaching our baseline checklist (PDF) — this is the version I typically use for first-pass validation.

High level next steps:
1) Medline provides IP allowlist, NAT pool(s), and the service account principal for the control-plane API.
2) Redwood runs a smoke traffic plan (connectivity, TLS negotiation, auth flow) in a preflight window.
3) If smoke passes, we move to test traffic and acceptance (30-minute window with synthetic load).

Immediate asks for your network ops team:
- Confirm NAT public IPs (we need at least 2 for high-availability NAT).
- Add our control-plane FQDN to your allowlist and ensure outbound to our telemetry endpoints (fqdn: telemetry.redwood-inference.com:443)
- Provide KMS contact and whether you prefer Cloud KMS or a bring-your-own-HSM model for key wrapping.

Ben, can you confirm the firewall ports (TCP) and whether we'll require BGP peering or static routes for the enclave upstream?

I can do a 30-minute sync on Monday afternoon if that works.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jun 1, 2028 at 12:04 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben, can you confirm the firewall ports (TCP) and whether we'll require BGP peering or static routes for the enclave upstream?

Quick tech breakdown from infra: (summary / minimum requirements)

1) Routing model
- Preferred: Static routes + NAT gateway for simplicity in initial stages.
- Optional: BGP peering for large scale or multi-AZ on-prem setups; we can support if Medline operations prefer dynamic routing.

2) NAT / Egress
- Provide 2x elastic public IPs for SNAT. These must be reserved for Redwood egress so our tokenized telemetry and proxy egress remain stable.

3) Ports and endpoints (minimum)
- Outbound: 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.com (TLS), 443 to api.redwood-inference.com (control-plane)
- Inbound: None required to the enclave unless you opt for tunneled debug access; if so, we will request a specific jump host IP and port range (SSH 22 / TLS 8443)

4) IAM / service accounts
- Create a service account for "redwood-deploy@[project]" with the following roles: KeyManager.Encrypt, Network.View, Logs.Writer (least-privilege list attached to network-smoke-test-steps.md)

5) KMS
- If using Cloud KMS, provide a key resource name and grant Redwood the Encrypt/Decrypt role on that key.
- For HSM, we'll need contact details for the HSM admin and any cert chains beforehand.

6) Smoke tests we will run during preflight
- TLS handshake and cert verification against provided certs
- Auth flow using provided service account token exchange
- Small synthetic inference call (1–2 requests) to validate model serving pipeline and latency baseline

Open items for Medline:
- Confirm whether egress must route through an internal proxy (we can run tests through the proxy but need proxy host/port + TLS root cert)
- Provide the KMS resource name or HSM contact

I've attached a short doc with the smoke test steps — it includes the exact CLI commands we use so your security team can review.

— Ben Carter
Infrastructure Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — great thread. I've consolidated Ben's notes into an environment-acceptance template and a short preflight script that we will run on the day-of. Attaching the CSV template for acceptance results and a link to the shared onboarding folder (see related links).

Final checklist summary (what we'll mark as "entry gate cleared"):
- NAT IPs reserved and handed off to Redwood
- Control-plane hostname reachable from Medline VPC (TLS verified)
- Service account provisioned and IAM roles granted
- KMS resource accessible with correct permissions
- Firewall rules allowing outbound 443 to telemetry and control endpoints
- Successful run of smoke tests with logs exported to the URL Medline provides

Please upload the completed env-acceptance-template.csv and any export logs to the Drive folder before our scheduled preflight window. If anything looks risky from a compliance side, flag it here and we'll scope a mitigation (canary ranges, additional auditing, or temporary rate limits).

I'll be on the call Monday at 2:30pm PT.

— Aditya Rao
Principal Engineer, Deployment Runtime | Redwood Inference
